g.text: Each line is one hash. Each dot is the median of up to 48 timings at that size.
A dot's shape marks the method the hash used at that size. The section "Code paths" at the bottom names each method.
Rate counts bytes or messages per second, time the nanoseconds per byte or message; the switch at right changes every plot.
The strip at the top narrows every plot to part of its inputs: drag an end of its band, or use the arrows at its ends.

After other work: the program calls the hash, runs a fixed other program (about 1 MiB of code) and reads 128 MiB of data, at least 1 ms in all, writes the input, and calls again; the second call is timed. So a program works that hashes between its other tasks.
After idling: the program calls the hash, sleeps 1 ms, writes the input, and calls again; the second call is timed. So a server works that waits for its next request.
Nonstop, each input (each 64 KiB piece of a message in pieces) is first read into memory, a memory copy, the cheapest read, inside the time.
Owned buffers: the program hands each buffer over and fills the next while it is hashed. Lent buffers: the program waits for each call to return before refilling its buffer.
Where a line splits in two, the timings ran at two different speeds; the note under the last plot says why.
A message in one buffer, after other work
the program hashes, runs other code and reads 128 MiB of memory, and hashes again; the time of the second call
Gigabytes per second (log scale) · higher is better

g.text: [*] Two speeds: at some sizes the timings fell into two clearly different speeds, so the line splits in two there, each speed drawn as strong
as its share of the timings. A common cause is a chip with fast performance cores and slower efficiency cores, where the operating
system may run the work on either kind. Two programs sharing one part of the chip, or a virtual machine its host moves between cores, split speeds too.

g.data-summary: the method behind each dot shape, hash by hash
g.text: ▾ Code paths — the method behind each dot shape, hash by hash
SHA-256 · ● the CPU's SHA-256 instructions, where it has them, from the start (one buffer, after other work, one buffer, after idling, messages, owned buffers, messages, lent
buffers, pieces, lent buffers): One method at every size.
SHA-256 · ● the CPU's SHA-256 instructions, where it has them, one message per call, from the start (a batch, after other work, a batch, after idling, batches, owned buffers,
batches, lent buffers): Each message is its own call; the size of the batch changes nothing.
BLAKE3 servil st · ● SSE4.1 compression, from the start (one buffer, after other work, one buffer, after idling, messages, lent buffers, pieces, lent buffers): Inputs of one
chunk (1 KiB) or less run one compression per block on the calling platform's compress kernel.
BLAKE3 servil st · ◆ AVX2 hash_many (8-way), from 1025 B (one buffer, after other work, one buffer, after idling, messages, lent buffers, pieces, lent buffers): Above one chunk
the tree is hashed several chunks at a time, up to the platform's SIMD degree per call.
BLAKE3 servil st · ● SSE4.1 compression, from the start (a batch, after other work, a batch, after idling, batches, lent buffers): A single message runs one compression per block
on the calling platform's compress kernel.
BLAKE3 servil st · ◆ AVX2 hash_many (8-way), from 2 messages (a batch, after other work, a batch, after idling, batches, lent buffers): Two or more messages are hashed together,
up to the platform's SIMD degree per call.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● SSE4.1 compression, from the start (one buffer, after other work, one buffer, after idling, messages, lent buffers): Inputs of one chunk (1 KiB) or less run
one compression per block on the calling platform's compress kernel.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ◆ AVX2 hash_many (8-way), from 1025 B (one buffer, after other work, one buffer, after idling, messages, lent buffers): Above one chunk the tree is hashed
several chunks at a time, up to the platform's SIMD degree per call.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ■ split over threads, SME2 on one for large inputs, from 512 KiB (one buffer, after other work, one buffer, after idling, messages, lent buffers): From here
the input is cut into whole subtrees that the calling thread and this crate's worker threads (one per CPU beyond the first) hash at once, the workers with integer and NEON code.
Once its share comes to 128 KiB or more (with sixteen threads, inputs from about 1.3 MiB), the calling thread hashes a share sized to its speed on SME2, with integer code beside
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● SSE4.1 compression, from the start (a batch, after other work, a batch, after idling, batches, lent buffers): A single message runs one compression per block
on the calling platform's compress kernel.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ◆ AVX2 hash_many (8-way), from 2 messages (a batch, after other work, a batch, after idling, batches, lent buffers): Two or more messages are hashed together,
up to the platform's SIMD degree per call.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ■ split over threads, from 8192 messages (a batch, after other work, a batch, after idling, batches, lent buffers): From here the batch is cut into ranges of
messages that the calling thread and this crate's worker threads (one per CPU beyond the first) hash at once, each with integer and NEON code.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● Queue::messages, from the start (messages, owned buffers): The contender leaves this API's kernel schedule unreported.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● Queue::pieces, from 65537 B (messages, owned buffers): The contender leaves this API's kernel schedule unreported.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● Queue::fixed, from the start (batches, owned buffers): The contender leaves this API's kernel schedule unreported.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● Hasher::update_multithreaded, from the start (pieces, lent buffers): The contender leaves this API's kernel schedule unreported.
